recall_prompt: Say how you would find the probability of 53 Sundays and of exactly 52 Sundays in a non-leap year — the extra day, the seven cases, and the two answers.
insider_note: A non-leap year is 52 full weeks plus ONE day; that one day fixes both answers. 52 Sundays "only" is the complement of 53, so it is 1 − 1/7 and not a fresh count.

steps.label: 52 weeks + 1 day; seven cases
steps.margin_note: First mark. 365 = 52 × 7 + 1. Every day of the week occurs 52 times; the one extra day can be any of the seven, equally likely.
steps.memory_tip: 365 = 52 × 7 + 1. Every weekday occurs 52 times; the ONE extra day decides everything.

common_mistakes: Using 366 days (a leap year has TWO extra days and a different answer).

steps.label: (i) 53 Sundays
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 53 Sundays happens only when the extra day is a Sunday: one case out of seven.
steps.memory_tip: 53 Sundays needs the extra day to be a Sunday — one case out of seven.

recall.must_convey: That 53 Sundays occurs only when the extra day is Sunday, so P = 1/7.

steps.why: The 53rd Sunday can only be the leftover day, so the favourable case is exactly one of the seven.

steps.label: (ii) 52 Sundays only
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Exactly 52 Sundays means the extra day is NOT a Sunday: the complement of (i), 1 − 1/7 = 6/7.
steps.memory_tip: '52 only' is the complement of part (i): 1 − 1/7 = 6/7, not a fresh count.
